name: Trick-or-Treat News
author: Loy Family Lights (fork of fpp-plugin-naughtynice by Joseph Jarboe)
description: Halloween 'Spooky News' broadcast for your LED matrix: trick-or-treater names, a TREAT/TRICK verdict, photo or costume art, and a scrolling ticker. Enter names from a phone on your Wi-Fi - no cloud needed.

privacy.summary: Locally accepts visitor names and costume selections and optional phone camera photos to display Halloween greetings on FPP. Stores submissions and photos on the controller. An optional administrator-configured cloud service can exchange submission data; it is inactive until configured.

sends.what: Cloud submissions and responses, including submitted names, costume information and potentially photos, depending on the configured service
sends.why: To retrieve and process optional cloud-based Trick-or-Treat submissions

collects.what: Visitor first names, costume selections, optional uploaded photos, and local submission queue/status
collects.where: On the FPP controller in the plugin private configuration and uploads directories
collects.why: To queue and display personalized greetings on the LED matrix

sensors.what: Optional visitor phone camera or photo library
sensors.why: Visitor-selected photo upload for display; no microphone use

systemChanges: Installs Python dependencies in a plugin virtual environment and a plugin-owned FPP shared display script; may create or change FPP Pixel Overlay Models and playlists only when the administrator explicitly runs zone setup; starts its own background daemon.
privacy.other: The door form is served by FPP over the network; anyone who can reach that form may submit a greeting. No internet exposure is configured by this plugin. Photo capture is optional and browser-initiated. The plugin does not automatically remove submitted data or plugin settings on uninstall; administrators should manage saved names and photos. Optional cloud access requires an administrator-supplied URL and token. Installer requires network access to install Python packages. The plugin source is publicly available on GitHub.
